customers.title: Selling 1 — Customers & Selling Foundations
customers.desc: The customer master done right: groups, territories, contacts and addresses, credit limits, and the Selling Settings that shape every document after it.

lessons.title: The Customer master
lessons.html:
Every selling document in ZhiftERP hangs off a Customer. Create one from Selling > Customer: the name, Customer Group, and Territory are the three fields that drive reporting later — group answers what kind of customer (Retail, Pharmacy, Distributor), territory answers where (Lagos Mainland, Abuja, South-West).

Set the Default Price List and Default Currency on the customer so quotations pick the right rates automatically. A customer created carelessly today is a reporting headache for years — the master record is a contract with your future reports.

lessons.title: Contacts & addresses
lessons.html:
A Customer is a company; the humans and locations attach separately. Contacts carry names, phones, and emails; Addresses carry billing and shipping locations. One customer can hold many of each — a chain like your larger retail accounts has one customer record and dozens of branch shipping addresses.

Mark one contact and one address as primary: documents pull them by default. When a quotation shows the wrong address, the fix is almost always the address record, not the quotation.

lessons.title: Credit limits & the credit controller
lessons.html:
A Credit Limit on the customer caps how much unpaid exposure you allow. When a new Sales Order would push the outstanding balance past the limit, ZhiftERP blocks submission.

Only a user holding the Credit Controller role can bypass the block — deliberately, per document. This is the difference between a sales team that grows revenue and one that grows bad debt: the limit is policy, the controller is the exception process.

lessons.title: Selling Settings that matter
lessons.html:
Selling Settings (search it in the awesome bar) holds the switches that shape daily work: customer naming, the default price list, whether sales staff must have an Item Price before selling, and whether one item can appear on multiple rows of the same order.

Two to know cold: Allow Item to be Added Multiple Times (same item at two rates on one order) and Maintain Same Rate Throughout Sales Cycle — which stops the delivery note quietly changing the price agreed on the order.

questions.q: Which three Customer fields most directly drive sales reporting in ZhiftERP?
opts: Customer Group, Territory, and the customer name
questions.why: Group and territory are the analysis dimensions every sales report slices by.

questions.q: A customer's quotations keep defaulting to the wrong currency. Where is the durable fix?
questions.why: Document defaults flow from the customer master — fix the master, not the symptom.

questions.q: One customer with 30 branches needing deliveries to each branch is modelled as:
opts: One customer, addresses typed per order
questions.why: One company = one customer; locations are address records attached to it.

questions.q: Documents pull which contact and address by default?
opts: The primary contact and primary address
questions.why: The primary flags control defaulting.

questions.q: A Sales Order is blocked because the customer would exceed their credit limit. Who can let it through?
opts: A user with the Credit Controller role
The sales user who made it
Nobody — it must be paid first
questions.why: Credit Controller is the deliberate bypass role for credit-limit blocks.

questions.q: The credit limit measures the customer's:
questions.why: It caps outstanding receivables, not sales volume.

questions.q: Where do you control whether the same item can appear on two rows of one order?
opts: Selling Settings — Allow Item to be Added Multiple Times
questions.why: It's a Selling Settings switch.

questions.q: "Maintain Same Rate Throughout Sales Cycle" protects against:
opts: The rate silently differing between order and delivery/invoice
questions.why: It enforces the agreed rate downstream through the cycle.

questions.q: Customer Group answers which question about a customer?
opts: What kind of customer they are
questions.why: Group is the kind/segment dimension; territory is the where.

questions.q: The right place to record a buyer's phone number is:
opts: A Contact linked to the customer
questions.why: People live on Contact records, linked to the customer.

questions.q: Territory on the customer is best set to:
opts: The geographic region used in your reporting structure
questions.why: Territory is the geography dimension for analysis and targets.

questions.q: A new customer record should always be created with:
opts: Name, group, territory, currency and default price list set deliberately
A copied address from another customer
questions.why: Master data created deliberately keeps every later document and report clean.

items_prices.title: Selling 2 — Items & Price Lists
items_prices.desc: Sellable items, units of measure, selling price lists and Item Prices — where every rate on every quotation actually comes from.

lessons.title: The sellable item
lessons.html: An Item must have Is Sales Item ticked to appear on selling documents. The Item Group plays the same reporting role Customer Group plays on the other side. The Default Unit of Measure (UOM) is the unit stock is kept in; a Sales UOM can differ — keep stock in Units, sell in Cartons of 12 — with a conversion factor doing the arithmetic.

lessons.title: Price lists
lessons.html:
A Price List is a named collection of rates in one currency — Standard Selling, Distributor NGN, Export USD. Selling documents read rates from the price list on the document, which defaults from the customer.

Price lists separate who pays what: the same item can be ₦1,000 on Retail and ₦850 on Distributor with no discounts involved — cleaner than discounting, because reports then show true agreed rates.

lessons.title: Item Price records
lessons.html:
The actual number lives in an Item Price: item + price list + rate (+ optional validity dates and minimum quantity). When a quotation row finds no Item Price for its price list, the rate comes up zero — the single most common "why is my rate 0?" answer in support.

Bulk price maintenance is an import job: export Item Prices, update rates in the sheet, re-import. Never retype fifty rates by hand.

lessons.title: Currency & conversion
lessons.html:
A price list has one currency. Quote a USD price list to a naira customer and ZhiftERP converts using the Currency Exchange rate into the document currency — visible on the document as the conversion rate.

Rule of thumb: one price list per currency per commercial arrangement, and let the customer default do the choosing.

questions.q: An item refuses to appear on a quotation. First thing to check:
opts: Is Sales Item is ticked on the item
questions.why: Only sales items appear on selling documents.

questions.q: Stock kept in Units but sold in Cartons of 12 uses:

questions.why: Sales UOM + conversion factor handles the unit difference.

questions.q: A quotation row shows rate 0. The most common cause:
opts: No Item Price exists for the document's price list
questions.why: Rates come from Item Price records; missing record = zero.

questions.q: Retail pays ₦1,000, distributors pay ₦850 for the same item. Cleanest model:
opts: Two price lists with their own Item Prices
Edit the rate manually each time
questions.why: Separate price lists show true agreed rates without discount noise.

questions.q: The rate a quotation uses comes from:
opts: The Item Price for the document's price list
questions.why: The document's price list is looked up in Item Price.

questions.q: A price list can contain:
questions.why: One price list, one currency.

questions.q: Updating 300 selling rates at quarter start is best done by:
opts: Export, update in sheet, re-import Item Prices
questions.why: Bulk price maintenance is an import job.

questions.q: Which field defaults the price list onto a new quotation?
questions.why: The customer default drives document defaulting.

questions.q: Item Group serves the same purpose for items that ______ serves for customers.
questions.why: Both are the segment/reporting dimension of their master.

questions.q: A USD price list on a naira document results in:
opts: Automatic conversion at the exchange rate into document currency
questions.why: Currency Exchange converts into the document currency.

questions.q: An Item Price can be limited by:
questions.why: Valid-from/upto and min qty scope an Item Price.

questions.q: The unit stock is counted in is the item's:
questions.why: Default UOM is the stock-keeping unit; Sales UOM is for selling.

quotations.title: Selling 3 — Quotations
quotations.desc: The offer document: creating quotations, validity, taxes on the offer, the status lifecycle, losing gracefully, and converting to an order.

lessons.title: Creating the offer
lessons.html:
A Quotation is the formal offer: customer (or lead), items, quantities, rates, taxes, terms. Create it directly from Selling > Quotation or from a CRM opportunity so the trail from first contact to offer stays linked.

Rates arrive from the price list; you can override per row — overrides are visible and reportable, so discipline stays intact. The Valid Till date says how long the offer stands; after it passes, the quotation shows Expired.

lessons.title: Taxes on the quotation
lessons.html:
Attach a Sales Taxes and Charges Template — for Nigerian trade, typically VAT at 7.5% — and the quotation shows the customer the true payable total. Quoting without tax and surprising the customer at invoice is how deals sour late.

The template travels forward: convert the quotation and the same taxes flow onto the Sales Order and beyond.

lessons.title: The status lifecycle
lessons.html: Draft → Open on submit. From Open: Ordered when a Sales Order is made from it, Lost when you concede, Expired when Valid Till passes, Cancelled if withdrawn. The Quotation list filtered to Open IS your offers-awaiting-answer pipeline — keep it honest.

lessons.title: Losing well & converting
lessons.html:
Marking a quotation Lost asks for a Lost Reason (price, competitor, timing). Six months of honest lost reasons is a strategy document nobody had to write.

Winning: Create > Sales Order from the quotation carries everything across — items, rates, taxes, terms — no retyping, no transcription errors. The quotation flips to Ordered and the chain of custody is unbroken.

questions.q: A submitted quotation awaiting the customer's answer shows status:

questions.why: Expiry is automatic from the Valid Till date.

questions.why: Lost reasons accumulate into competitive intelligence.

questions.why: The tax template carries VAT onto the document.

questions.q: Why quote taxes on the offer rather than adding them at invoice?
opts: The customer sees the true payable total — no late surprises
questions.why: Late tax surprises sour closed deals.

questions.why: Row overrides are permitted and transparent.

opts: Items, rates, taxes and terms carry over with no transcription errors
questions.why: Document flow preserves the agreed offer exactly.

questions.q: A quotation can be made against:
questions.why: Quotations support leads as well as customers.

opts: Must be re-entered on the order
Flow onto the Sales Order made from it

questions.q: Six months of Lost Reasons is best used as:
opts: Competitive and pricing intelligence for strategy
questions.why: Patterns in why deals die tell you what to fix.

sales_orders.title: Selling 4 — Sales Orders
sales_orders.desc: The commitment document: delivery dates, what submission reserves, the status language, amendments, holds and closes, and delivery tolerance.

lessons.title: The commitment
lessons.html: A Sales Order is the point where an offer becomes an obligation: the customer has said yes, and you now owe goods by the Delivery Date. Made from the quotation (preferred) or directly, it carries items, rates, taxes, and per-row delivery dates when different lines ship at different times.

lessons.title: What submission does
lessons.html: Submitting a Sales Order commits stock intent: ordered quantities appear as reserved against the warehouse, so planners and other salespeople see the truth of what is promised. It also opens the order's fulfilment ledger — every delivery note and invoice made from it counts down the remaining quantities.

lessons.title: Status language & control
lessons.html:
A submitted order reads To Deliver and Bill, then To Bill (delivered, not invoiced), To Deliver (invoiced first), and Completed. Two manual controls: Hold pauses an order (credit issues, stock trouble) and Close ends it early — the customer took 80 of 100 and won't take more; closing releases the reservation and stops the order haunting your pending lists.

Amending: cancel and Amend creates the next revision with full history preserved.

lessons.title: Delivery tolerance
lessons.html: Real warehouses ship 102 units against an order of 100. The Over Delivery/Receipt Allowance % (on the item or globally) says how much overage a delivery may carry before ZhiftERP blocks it. Zero tolerance means exact quantities only — right for serialized goods, wrong for bulk.

questions.q: A freshly submitted, untouched Sales Order shows status:
questions.why: Both obligations — deliver and bill — are outstanding.

questions.q: Delivered in full but not yet invoiced, the order reads:
questions.why: Delivery done; billing remains.

questions.q: Submitting a Sales Order affects stock by:
opts: Reserving the ordered quantities against the warehouse
questions.why: Reservation shows everyone what's promised.

questions.q: The customer took 80 of 100 and will take no more. Correct action:
questions.why: Close ends it early, releases reservation, keeps history.

questions.q: An order that must pause for a credit issue should be:
questions.why: Hold pauses without destroying the commitment.

questions.q: Changing a submitted order's quantities is done by:
opts: Cancel then Amend, creating the next revision
Asking a System Manager to edit SQL
questions.why: Amend preserves the revision history.

questions.q: Shipping 102 against an order of 100 is permitted when:
opts: Over Delivery Allowance % covers the 2% overage
questions.why: The allowance defines acceptable overage before blocking.

questions.q: Different lines shipping at different times are handled by:
opts: Per-row delivery dates on one order
questions.why: Row-level delivery dates schedule split fulfilment.

questions.q: The order's remaining-to-deliver quantities count down as:
opts: Delivery Notes are made from the order
questions.why: Fulfilment documents made FROM the order drive its ledger.

questions.q: "To Deliver" (without "and Bill") means:
opts: Invoiced ahead of delivery; goods still owed
questions.why: Billing done first; delivery outstanding.

questions.q: Zero over-delivery tolerance is right for:

questions.why: Serialized goods need exact quantities; bulk needs slack.

questions.q: The preferred origin of a Sales Order is:
questions.why: Creating from the quotation preserves the agreed offer.

delivery.title: Selling 5 — Delivery Notes & Returns
delivery.desc: Where stock actually moves: delivery notes from orders, partial shipments, statuses, sales returns, packing slips, and serial/batch discipline.

lessons.title: The document that moves stock
lessons.html: The Delivery Note is the moment goods leave: submitting it deducts stock from the warehouse and counts down the Sales Order. Always create it from the order (Create > Delivery Note) so quantities, rates and taxes flow and the order's ledger stays true.

lessons.title: Partial delivery & status
lessons.html: Deliver 60 of 100 today: make the DN from the order and edit quantities down — the order remembers 40 remain, and the next DN offers exactly the 40 remaining. A DN reads To Bill until invoiced, then Completed; a DN can also be made against the invoice when billing led.

lessons.title: Sales returns
lessons.html: Goods come back via a Sales Return: a Delivery Note with Is Return ticked, made against the original DN, with negative quantities. Submitting it puts stock back into the warehouse and the paper trail ties the return to the exact original shipment. The money side is the credit note — a return Sales Invoice — covered in the next module.

lessons.title: Packing slips, serials & batches
lessons.html: A Packing Slip against the DN lists cartons and contents for the driver and the gate. Items tracked by Serial No or Batch demand the exact serials/batches on the DN — this is what makes "which customer got batch B-204?" answerable during a recall, in seconds instead of days.

questions.q: Stock is deducted from the warehouse at which moment?
questions.why: The DN is the stock-moving document.

questions.q: A Delivery Note should be created:
opts: From the Sales Order via Create > Delivery Note
questions.why: Creating from the order keeps the fulfilment ledger true.

questions.q: 60 of 100 delivered today. The next DN from the order will offer:
questions.why: The order tracks the remaining 40 automatically.

questions.q: An undelivered-quantity view across all orders lives in:
opts: The Sales Order's remaining quantities (and order analysis reports)
questions.why: Remaining-to-deliver is order-side data.

questions.q: A sales return is recorded as:
opts: A Delivery Note with Is Return, against the original DN, negative quantities
questions.why: The return DN reverses stock with a trail to the original.

questions.q: Submitting a sales-return DN moves stock:
questions.why: Returns restore stock.

questions.q: The customer-money side of a return is handled by:
questions.why: Stock and money reverse on separate linked documents.

questions.q: A DN that has shipped but not been invoiced reads:
questions.why: To Bill = goods gone, billing pending.

questions.q: "Which customers received batch B-204?" is answerable because:
opts: Batch numbers are recorded on each Delivery Note
questions.why: Batch/serial capture on the DN powers recall tracing.

questions.q: The Packing Slip exists to:
opts: List cartons and contents for the driver and the gate
questions.why: It's the physical-handling companion to the DN.

questions.q: A serial-tracked item on a DN requires:
opts: The exact serial numbers being shipped
questions.why: Serialized stock demands per-unit identity on the DN.

questions.q: A Delivery Note can also be created against:

questions.why: Invoice-first flows make the DN from the invoice.

taxes_invoicing.title: Selling 6 — Taxes, Pricing Rules & Invoicing
taxes_invoicing.desc: VAT done right, inclusive vs exclusive, item tax overrides, pricing rules and discounts, the Sales Invoice, payments, credit notes — and the reports that watch it all.

lessons.title: Sales taxes & VAT
lessons.html:
The Sales Taxes and Charges Template defines tax rows once — Nigerian VAT 7.5% output tax to its ledger account — and every selling document applies it consistently. An Item Tax Template on an item overrides the document rate for that row: how zero-rated or exempt items sit correctly on a VAT-able invoice.

Inclusive tax means the entered rate already contains VAT (₦1,075 inclusive = ₦1,000 + ₦75); exclusive adds it on top. Mixing them up misstates either your price or your VAT return.

lessons.title: Pricing rules & discounts
lessons.html:
A Pricing Rule applies a discount or special rate automatically when conditions match — item/group/brand, customer/group/territory, quantity brackets, validity dates. "10% off cartons of 50+ for Distributors in Q4" becomes a rule, not a memo.

Manual discounting still exists per document — the Additional Discount on totals or per-row rate cuts — but rules are policy while manual discounts are exceptions; keep the exceptional rare and visible.

lessons.title: The Sales Invoice & getting paid
lessons.html:
The Sales Invoice is the accounting event: submitting it books revenue and the customer's receivable. Make it from the order or the DN so quantities and taxes flow. Its outstanding amount clears via Payment Entry — full, partial, or one payment across several invoices.

Status tells the collection story: Unpaid, Partly Paid, Paid, Overdue once the due date passes — the Overdue filter is your collections worklist.

lessons.title: Credit notes & the watching reports
lessons.html:
A credit note is a Sales Invoice with Is Return — against the original invoice — reversing revenue and receivable for returned goods or corrections, mirroring the return DN on the money side.

Then the instruments: Sales Analytics (revenue by customer/item/territory over time), Sales Order Analysis (delivery backlog), and Accounts Receivable (who owes what, aged). A sales professional reads these weekly, not at quarter-end panic.

A discount equal to the VAT

questions.why: The invoice is the accounting event.

questions.why: Stock reverses on the return DN; money on the credit note.

sales_invoice.title: Selling 7 — The Sales Invoice, Payments & Collections
sales_invoice.desc: The accounting event in full: creating invoices from orders and delivery notes, what submission books, due dates and payment terms, Payment Entry mechanics including advances and allocation, credit notes, and the receivables discipline that turns sales into cash.

lessons.title: The invoice as the accounting event
lessons.html:
Everything before it was commitment and movement; the Sales Invoice is where money becomes real. Submitting it books revenue and the customer's receivable into the ledgers on its posting date. Make it from the Sales Order (billing before or alongside delivery) or from the Delivery Note (billing what actually shipped) — either way quantities, rates and taxes flow and the order's billed-quantity ledger counts down.

Two dates matter and are not the same: the posting date is when the books record it; the due date is when the customer must pay — computed from the Payment Terms (Net 30, 50% advance / 50% on delivery, and so on). Terms belong on the customer or the order so the invoice inherits them instead of someone deciding at billing time.

lessons.title: Statuses & the collections story
lessons.html:
An invoice's status is the collections narrative in one word: Unpaid when submitted, Partly Paid as money arrives, Paid when cleared, Overdue the moment the due date passes unpaid, and Credit Note Issued when a return has been raised against it. The invoice list filtered to Overdue, sorted oldest first, IS the collections worklist — a sales professional opens it weekly, not when cash runs short.

One special case to know: an invoice with Update Stock ticked moves inventory itself — used when the delivery note step is skipped (counter sales, services with materials). In the standard flow the DN moves stock and the invoice moves money; don't tick Update Stock on an invoice made from a DN or stock moves twice.

lessons.title: Payment Entry mechanics
lessons.html:
Money is recorded with a Payment Entry — made from the invoice so the reference and allocation come pre-filled. It handles every real-world shape: a full payment closes the invoice; a partial payment leaves it Partly Paid with the outstanding visible; one payment across several invoices is a single entry allocated over each reference; small shortfalls can be written off within your write-off limit instead of chasing ₦150 forever.

Advances work in reverse order: a Payment Entry taken against the customer before the invoice exists sits as an advance, then gets allocated to the invoice when raised — the 50%-upfront deals your enterprise clients sign are exactly this mechanic. Mode of Payment and the bank account on the entry are what make bank reconciliation painless later.

lessons.title: Credit notes & receivables discipline
lessons.html:
Corrections and returns reverse through a credit note — a Sales Invoice with Is Return against the original — pulling revenue and receivable back with a paper trail; the original flips to Credit Note Issued. Never "fix" a submitted invoice by editing history: the credit-note-plus-reinvoice pattern is what auditors, and FIRS, expect to find.

Discipline is the difference between sales and cash: the Accounts Receivable report ages who-owes-what into buckets (0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+); a Statement of Account sent monthly keeps customers honest; and every overdue invoice should have a next follow-up — which in this house means a dated next step on the Duty Board pipeline, not a hope.

questions.why: The invoice is the accounting event; earlier documents commit and move stock.

questions.why: Overdue is the past-due status — and the collections filter.

questions.why: Small differences write off; the invoice closes honestly.

opts: Credit note against it, then re-invoice correctly

advanced.title: Selling 8 — Advanced Selling: Settings, Bundles, Blanket Orders & Sales Teams
advanced.desc: The advanced layer: Selling Settings in depth, Product Bundles, Blanket Orders for long-term rate agreements, and the two sales-team structures — Sales Person (internal, contribution and targets) and Sales Partner (external channel and commission).

lessons.title: Selling Settings — the full tour
lessons.html:
Selling Settings is where selling policy becomes system behaviour; a consultant should be able to defend every switch. The naming pair — Customer Naming By (name vs naming series) — decides whether customers are "Alpha Pharmacy" or "CUST-00042"; chains with duplicate branch names need the series. Default Customer Group, Default Territory, and the default Selling Price List pre-fill every new record — set them to your commonest case so lazy data entry lands correctly.

The discipline switches: Maintain Same Rate Throughout Sales Cycle (the agreed rate can't drift between order, delivery, and invoice — and its companion action setting decides whether a drift is a hard Stop or just a Warning); Allow User to Edit Price List Rate (untick it and rates come only from Item Prices — the strongest anti-"special price" control you have); Validate Selling Price Against Purchase Rate (blocks selling below cost — margin protection at the point of entry); Allow Item to be Added Multiple Times; and the global over-delivery allowance that Module 4's per-item tolerance falls back to. Policy questions from clients — "can we stop staff discounting?", "can we prevent below-cost sales?" — are usually answered in this one screen.

lessons.title: Product Bundles
lessons.html:
A Product Bundle sells several stock items as one line: a "Pharmacy Starter Pack" parent containing shelf units, a scanner, and a printer. The parent item is non-stock (it never has warehouse quantity — untick Maintain Stock); the bundle definition lists the child items and quantities.

The mechanics to remember: the customer sees and pays the parent's price (one line, one rate on the quotation and invoice), while the Delivery Note explodes the bundle into its packed items — the children — and it's the children that move stock from the warehouse. Hampers, promo packs, starter kits, install kits: whenever you price as one thing but pick as many things, it's a bundle — never a workaround item with stock nobody counts.

lessons.title: Blanket Orders
lessons.html:
A Blanket Order is a long-term rate-and-quantity agreement: the customer commits to, say, 10,000 cartons over six months at ₦820 — better than rack rate, weaker than an order for everything at once. Create the blanket order with items, agreed quantities, rates, and the from/to dates.

Individual Sales Orders are then drawn against it: reference the blanket order and the row inherits the agreed rate automatically, and the blanket order tracks its drawdown — ordered quantity against committed quantity — so both sides see how much of the commitment remains. Use it instead of stretching a quotation's validity for months: a quotation is an offer awaiting an answer; a blanket order is an agreement being consumed.

lessons.title: Sales Person — the internal team
lessons.html:
Sales Person models your own team as a tree — Sales Director → Regional Managers → Field Reps — so results roll up the hierarchy. On a transaction, the Sales Team section assigns one or more sales persons each with a contribution % (summing to 100): a deal worked by two reps splits credit 60/40 and reports show each person's contributed revenue, not double-counted totals.

Set targets per sales person (by item group and period) and read the Sales Person-wise Transaction Summary against them — commissions, league tables, and performance conversations all come from this structure. If a client asks "can we see sales by rep?", the honest answer is: only if sales persons are assigned on documents — the discipline precedes the report.

lessons.title: Sales Partner — the external channel
lessons.html:
A Sales Partner is outside your company — a reseller, referral agent, or channel distributor who brings the deal — carrying a commission rate. Selecting the partner on a Sales Order or Invoice stamps the channel and computes the total commission on that document automatically.

The distinction to keep sharp: Sales Person is your staff (tree, contribution %, targets); Sales Partner is an external business (flat entity, commission %). A transaction can carry both — your rep worked the deal a referral partner introduced. The Sales Partner-wise Transaction Summary totals each channel's business and owed commission — pay partners from the report, not from their claims.

questions.q: A retail chain has many branches with similar names. Customer Naming By should be:
questions.why: Series naming avoids collisions and keeps records unambiguous.

questions.q: The strongest control to stop staff typing "special prices" on documents is:
opts: Unticking Allow User to Edit Price List Rate
questions.why: Rates then come only from Item Price records.

questions.q: Blocking sales below cost at the point of entry uses:
opts: Validate Selling Price Against Purchase Rate
questions.why: The validation setting is margin protection built into entry.

questions.q: Maintain Same Rate Throughout Sales Cycle can be configured to respond to a drift with:
opts: A Stop or a Warning, per the action setting
questions.why: The companion action setting chooses hard block vs warning.

questions.q: A Product Bundle's parent item must be:
questions.why: The parent is never counted in the warehouse; only children are.

questions.q: On a bundle sale, warehouse stock is deducted for:
opts: The packed child items on the Delivery Note
questions.why: The DN explodes the bundle; children move stock.

questions.q: The customer's invoice for a bundle shows:
opts: One line at the parent's price
questions.why: Price lives on the parent; picking lives on the children.

questions.q: A customer commits to 10,000 cartons over six months at an agreed rate. Model it as:
opts: A Blanket Order drawn down by individual Sales Orders
questions.why: Blanket orders are consumed agreements; quotations are offers.

questions.q: A Sales Order drawn against a blanket order inherits:
opts: The agreed rate, while the blanket tracks drawdown
questions.why: Rate flows from the agreement; drawdown is tracked against commitment.

questions.q: How much of a blanket commitment remains is read from:
questions.why: The blanket order itself tracks its consumption.

questions.q: Two reps split a deal 60/40. This is recorded via:
opts: Sales Team rows with contribution percentages summing to 100
questions.why: Contribution % splits credit without double-counting revenue.

questions.q: Sales Person is structured as:
opts: A tree so results roll up the hierarchy
questions.why: The tree gives regional and directorial roll-ups.

questions.q: "Show me sales by rep" only works if:
opts: Sales persons are assigned on the transactions
questions.why: The discipline of assignment precedes the report.

questions.q: Sales Person vs Sales Partner — the distinction is:
opts: Person is internal staff with contribution %; Partner is an external business with commission %
questions.why: Internal tree vs external channel — a document can carry both.

questions.q: Commission owed to a reseller is paid from:
questions.why: Pay channels from the system's totals, not their invoices' claims.
